verdict.rationale: SharePoint's docs name an official development framework, the SharePoint Framework (SPFx), for building web parts, extensions and Copilot UX components. That counts as first-party SDK-style tooling, but the pack covers it only briefly. The remaining evidence describes raw REST and Microsoft Graph HTTP APIs rather than official client libraries. Missing for 10: documented official client-library SDKs (e.g., language packages wrapping the REST/Graph APIs), SPFx depth (install, tooling, versions), and independent or hands-on corroboration of building with the SDKs.

support.subject: As an AI-native user, I can build against official SDKs

citations.quote: Build Copilot UX components, web parts, extensions, and business solutions with SharePoint Framework and Microsoft 365.
For SharePoint Online, use SPFx for user interface extensions
